## 1.1 The 2026 CRE Threat Environment

## Introduction

The global trajectory of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has entered a phase of epidemiological acceleration that is no longer adequately captured by decade-scale projections. While the 2019 Global Burden of Disease study attributed approximately 4.95 million deaths to bacterial AMR—with carbapenem resistance specifically identified among the leading contributors—current surveillance data from 2026 indicate that this baseline has already been exceeded in several high-incidence regions [6], [5]. Among the resistance phenotypes tracked, carbapenem-resistant *Enterobacteriaceae* (CRE) represent the most clinically intractable threat because they occupy the final therapeutic frontier of the β-lactam class and disseminate through both clonal expansion and horizontal plasmid transfer. The organisms most frequently implicated—carbapenem-resistant *Klebsiella pneumoniae* and *Escherichia coli*—are now endemic in hospital networks across the EU/EEA, with the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) formally classifying the risk of further spread as **high-to-very-high** [6].
